report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**.

### Evidence Summary

* **Clinical Trial Efficacy:** A major clinical trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* demonstrated that administering tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) starting in the third trimester (around week 28–32 of gestation) to pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus (HBV) viral loads significantly reduces mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1508660). Daily TDF treatment reduced the rate of perinatal transmission from 18% in the control group to 5% in the treatment group when combined with standard infant immunoprophylaxis (https://nyulangone.org/news/antiviral-treatment-during-pregnancy-reduces-mother-child-transmission-hepatitis-b).
* **Global Guidelines:** World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines explicitly recommend TDF antiviral prophylaxis starting at the 28th week of pregnancy for HBV-infected pregnant individuals with high maternal viral loads (HBV DNA $\ge 5.3 \text{ log}_{10}\text{ IU/mL}$ / $200,000\text{ IU/mL}$ or HBeAg positivity) to prevent vertical transmission (https://inserm.hal.science/inserm-04546100v1/document).
* **Current Clinical Practice:** Randomized controlled trials in journals such as *JAMA* affirm that third-trimester (gestational week 28) TDF initiation remains a widely accepted and highly effective strategy to prevent HBV MTCT alongside post-delivery infant vaccination (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2826316).
